Last mile is the costliest mile: route density, delivery promise, failed-delivery economics and urban access rules. Dynamic routing, fleet telemetry and micro-hub orchestration decide whether the final mile makes money.

Governance inherits the sector frame — Urban access/LEZ rules among others — with evidence generated by the delivery itself.

items: Facilities that run themselves: BMS/IoT fusion, energy optimization and city-scale platforms.

Simulate before you cut steel: plant, fleet and product twins with governed physics and data.

blocks.x: At industry level, the same pattern

At Logistics & Supply Chain level this capability reads as: gate, yard and dock telemetry into appointment systems (dwell time down 25-40%). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

Delivery runs on one weekly rhythm for every program of this type. Weeks 1–2 measure and sign the baseline with your team; nothing builds against an unsigned number. Weeks 3–8 prove the pattern on deliberately bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — under a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked into runbooks, monitoring and enablement, closing with a measured delta against the baseline. Every gate is pass, stop or redirect, in writing.
